rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2<U+2013>2.3 <U+2014> continuous open-path eddy-covariance measurements of carbon and water fluxes at the Daman maize site, 2012<U+2013>2018, plus soil moisture, meteorology and MODIS data. Q2: Section 3.2, Table 2, Figure 7 <U+2014> annual ET averaged 733 vs 640 kg H2O m-2 before and after the switch from flood to drip irrigation (about 13% lower), ecosystem WUE rose from 1.84 to 2.01<U+2013>2.09 g C kg-1 H2O (+9.3 to +13.6%) and canopy WUE by about 11%, with GPP essentially unchanged (<U+2212>0.16 to <U+2212>3.96%); Section 4.2/Conclusions state drip irrigation saved water and raised WUE in this maize cropland. Q4: Table 2 and Sections 3.2, 4.2 <U+2014> ET partitioned into T and E (soil evaporation fell about 9<U+2013>20%, T 11<U+2013>14%) and soil moisture measured at 4, 40 and 160 cm, with deep-layer moisture 36<U+2013>42% lower under drip, interpreted as reduced wetting depth and deep percolation; model partitioning validated against 2012 lysimeter and isotope data (Figure 2).
rows.notes: Design is a before/after comparison at a single flux tower (flood 2012<U+2013>2016 vs drip under film mulch 2017<U+2013>2018), not a controlled side-by-side trial; mulch was present under both regimes, so the contrast is drip vs flood. Water saving is inferred from lower ET and soil moisture; drip irrigation volumes are not reported. Q3: the drip-vs-flood result rests on the EC time series (lysimeter/isotope data only in 2012, used for model validation) <U+2014> one method. Q7: authors attribute the effect to deficit amount and higher frequency of drip and to film mulch, and note 2017 high-intensity drip raised surface moisture, but these are not stated as requirements. Q8: the only caveat is the Table 2 note that drip intensity differed between 2017 and 2018, so two data subsets were used; no explicit limitation of the before/after design or single site. Q9: the <U+00B1> values (1.90 <U+00B1> 0.17, Table 1 SDs) describe interannual means, not the drip effect; the 9<U+2013>14% figure is a range between two data subsets rather than a dispersion measure.
